event: Nala tells Wat no one is hunting her, but she is owned by no village either.

changes.note: Wat: a straight answer on hunting, and her village shared, earn 2

memory.fact: No one is hunting Nala, but she is owned by no village.
No one is hunting Nala, but she is owned by no village.

event: She says that may make the village unsafe for her, and asks if there is any other way to heal.
She asks whether more levels, or better stats, would be enough to mend her.
Wat grunts at "hunting", as if a stone has been set down that he was carrying.
He answers the level question first, and flatly: a level makes you harder, not whole.
He says a hurt still wants rest and care, whatever the letters say; a leveled man bleeds the same.

memory.fact: The burners hold that a level makes you harder, not whole; a hurt still wants rest and care.
The burners hold that a level makes you harder, not whole; a hurt still wants rest and care.

event: Rest heals, he says: sleep under a roof, eat, and keep off that foot, and a body mends itself.
He says the temple at Wenmarch heals with light, for silver, and that is two days on past the ford.

memory.fact: The temple at Wenmarch heals with light, for silver; it lies two days on past the ford.
The temple at Wenmarch heals with light, for silver; it lies two days on past the ford.

event: Neither of them, he says, has silver to spare for a stranger's foot, and he says it without shame.
Jory comes back in for the kettle, and Wat tells him what she said about the village.

changes.note: Jory: her straight answer on hunting and her village earn 2

memory.fact: No one is hunting Nala, but she is owned by no village.

event: Jory thinks about it with the kettle in his hand; then he says he is a Brackenford man.
He says his mother is headwoman there, and one he speaks for goes through the gate unasked.

memory.fact: Jory Tull is a Brackenford man, and his mother is Brackenford's headwoman.
Jory Tull is a Brackenford man, and his mother is Brackenford's headwoman.
One vouched for by a Brackenford man is let through the gate without the questions.
One vouched for by a Brackenford man is let through the gate without the questions.

event: Wat says guest-right is a night and a breakfast; after that it is work, pay or the road.

memory.fact: Guest-right lasts the night and the morning meal; longer means work, pay or the road.
Guest-right lasts the night and the morning meal; longer means work, pay or the road.

event: He slaps his knee and says his knees are bad for sitting the clamp at night.
Someone has to sit up with it and call out if it flares, and he would sooner sleep.

memory.fact: The clamp needs a night watcher to call if it flares; Wat's knees make the night hard on him.
The clamp needs a night watcher to call if it flares; Wat's knees make the night hard on him.

event: He says a guest who sits the night watch eats at this fire till the raft goes down.

memory.fact: A guest who sits the clamp's night watch earns her keep at the camp until the raft goes.
A guest who sits the clamp's night watch earns her keep at the camp until the raft goes.

event: Jory says that in five days she would ride the raft to Brackenford with them, spoken for.

memory.fact: The burners offer Nala keep for the night watch, then the raft to Brackenford in five days.
The burners offer Nala keep for the night watch, then the raft to Brackenford in five days.

event: Wat looks at her across the fire and asks whether she can sit awake in the dark and not panic.
